items.definition: Root cause analysis finds the underlying cause of a problem — the one that, if removed, stops it recurring — rather than the first visible symptom.
items.definition_ar: تحليل السبب الجذري يبحث عن السبب الأساسي للمشكلة، الذي إذا أزيل لا تتكرر، وليس أول عرض ظاهر لها.
items.explanation: Steps: state the problem precisely (what, where, when, how much); collect evidence (events, documents, timestamps); list candidate causes; test each against the evidence; confirm the cause by showing the fix works; record it. A cause is only 'confirmed' when the evidence proves it — otherwise it is likely, possible or unknown, and should be called that.

items.definition: The five whys asks 'why?' repeatedly, each answer becoming the next question, until a cause that can be acted on is reached.
items.definition_ar: أسلوب لماذا الخمس يكرر السؤال 'لماذا؟' بحيث تصبح كل إجابة سؤالًا جديدًا حتى الوصول لسبب يمكن معالجته.
items.example: Demurrage on container X. Why? Not collected within free time. Why? Customs release was late. Why? The declaration was amended. Why? The invoice weight differed from the B/L. Why? The supplier invoiced before final packing. Action: invoice after packing, or agree a weight check before shipment.
limitations: Each 'because' needs evidence; a chain of guesses ends in a confident wrong answer.
Real problems often have several contributing causes.

items.definition: A fishbone diagram groups candidate causes of one problem under headings — for logistics often people, process, documents, carrier, systems and external factors — so none is overlooked.
items.definition_ar: مخطط عظم السمكة يجمع الأسباب المحتملة لمشكلة واحدة تحت عناوين (في اللوجستيات غالبًا: الأفراد، الإجراءات، المستندات، الناقل، الأنظمة، العوامل الخارجية) حتى لا يُغفل أي منها.

items.definition: Correlation means two things move together; causation means one produces the other. Logistics data is full of correlations that are not causes.
items.definition_ar: الارتباط يعني أن شيئين يتغيران معًا، والسببية تعني أن أحدهما يُحدث الآخر، وبيانات اللوجستيات مليئة بارتباطات ليست أسبابًا.
items.explanation: Carrier A's shipments are later than carrier B's — but if A carries the hard lanes (transshipment, congested ports), the lane is the confounder, not the carrier. To argue causation: the cause comes before the effect, a plausible mechanism exists, the effect holds when other factors are held equal (same lane, mode, period), and removing the cause removes the effect.
items.example: More customs holds in December correlates with more shipments, not necessarily with worse documents: compare the hold rate, not the count.

items.definition: When the available evidence does not establish an answer, the correct answer is to say so, state what is known, list the possible explanations as hypotheses, and name the evidence that would decide between them.
items.definition_ar: عندما لا تكفي الأدلة المتاحة لإثبات إجابة، فالإجابة الصحيحة أن يُقال ذلك، مع ذكر المعلوم، وعرض التفسيرات المحتملة كفرضيات، وتحديد الدليل الذي يحسم بينها.
items.explanation: ATLAS never invents a shipment status, a carrier's reason for a delay, a regulation or a cause. 'The carrier gave no reason; possible causes are X or Y; the carrier's schedule notice or the booking history would tell' is a complete, useful answer.

sources.note: The CONFIRMED / LIKELY / POSSIBLE / UNKNOWN evidence ranking ATLAS uses for failures.

items.definition: Recovery planning decides how to limit the damage of a disruption: what can still be saved, the options with their cost, time and risk, who decides, and how success will be checked.
items.definition_ar: تخطيط التعافي يحدد كيفية الحد من ضرر الاضطراب: ما الذي يمكن إنقاذه، والخيارات بتكلفتها وزمنها ومخاطرها، ومن يقرر، وكيف يُتحقق من النجاح.
items.explanation: Typical levers: expedite clearance (pre-lodge documents, pay duties early), switch mode for the urgent part of the order (air a few critical parts, leave the rest by sea), reroute, use stock from another branch, renegotiate the customer date early. Act on the bottleneck, not on everything.

items.definition: Alternative routing is moving a shipment (or the rest of a flow) by a different route, port, carrier or mode to avoid a disruption.
items.definition_ar: إعادة التوجيه هي نقل الشحنة أو بقية التدفق عبر مسار أو ميناء أو ناقل أو وسيلة مختلفة لتجنب اضطراب ما.
items.explanation: Compare door-to-door: a faster sailing to a different port may lose its gain in inland transport or a second clearance. Rerouting cargo already on board is usually limited and costly (diversion fees, new documents); it is mostly a decision for cargo not yet shipped.

items.definition: Comparing carriers fairly means comparing them on the same lanes, modes, service levels and period, with enough shipments in each comparison, and on several measures — not a single average.
items.definition_ar: المقارنة العادلة بين الناقلين تكون على نفس المسارات والوسائل ومستويات الخدمة والفترة، بعدد كافٍ من الشحنات، وعلى عدة مقاييس لا متوسط واحد.
items.explanation: Report 'not enough data' for small samples. In this platform, a carrier's automation success rate also reflects its website (verification checks, layout changes), which is not the same as its transport performance; keep the two apart.

items.definition: Diagnosing a documentation exception means finding which document, which field and which party: compare the invoice, packing list, transport document, certificate of origin and declaration field by field against each other and against the importer's registration.
items.definition_ar: تشخيص مشكلة المستندات يعني تحديد أي مستند وأي حقل وأي طرف: مقارنة الفاتورة وقائمة التعبئة ومستند النقل وشهادة المنشأ والإقرار حقلًا بحقل مع بعضها ومع تسجيل المستورد.
items.explanation: Fix at the source: a wrong B/L needs a carrier amendment (time and fee), a wrong invoice needs the supplier, a wrong declaration the broker. Record which party caused it to prevent recurrence.

items.definition: Diagnosing a customs exception means establishing which stage stopped (declaration, assessment, inspection, payment, other agency, release), why, who must act, and the deadline that matters (usually the last free day).
items.definition_ar: تشخيص مشكلة الجمارك يعني تحديد المرحلة المتوقفة (الإقرار، التقدير، المعاينة، السداد، جهة أخرى، الإفراج) وسببها ومن عليه التصرف والموعد المهم (عادة آخر يوم سماح).
items.explanation: Ask the customs system or broker for the actual status before acting; carrier tracking only shows that clearance is in progress or on hold. In the Clearance page the current step and its days past due show which stage is late and who the clearing agent is.

items.definition: Risk prioritisation ranks issues by impact × likelihood (and urgency), so effort goes first where the expected damage is greatest.
items.definition_ar: ترتيب الأولويات حسب المخاطر يرتب المشكلات حسب الأثر × الاحتمال (والإلحاح) لتوجيه الجهد أولًا حيث الضرر المتوقع أكبر.
items.explanation: In clearance work, impact is the customer and cost consequence (a machine-down part, demurrage accruing); urgency is time to the next deadline (last free day). A shipment 30 days past due but with no charges running may rank below one 2 days past due whose free time ends tomorrow.

items.definition: Impact assessment states what a disruption means for the business: which orders and customers are affected, the cost (charges, expediting, lost sales), the time, and any safety or compliance consequence.
items.definition_ar: تقييم الأثر يوضح ماذا يعني الاضطراب للعمل: الطلبات والعملاء المتأثرون، والتكلفة (رسوم، تسريع، مبيعات ضائعة)، والوقت، وأي أثر على السلامة أو الامتثال.

items.definition: Scenario analysis works out the consequences of a few plausible futures (best, expected, worst) so a decision holds up whichever happens.
items.definition_ar: تحليل السيناريوهات يحسب نتائج عدة مستقبلات محتملة (الأفضل، المتوقع، الأسوأ) ليصمد القرار أيًا كان ما يحدث.

items.definition: Supply risk assessment identifies what could interrupt supply (supplier failure, port closure, capacity crunch, regulation change), estimates likelihood and impact, and plans buffers or alternatives; forecasting supplies the expected demand those plans must meet.
items.definition_ar: تقييم مخاطر الإمداد يحدد ما قد يقطع الإمداد (تعثر مورد، إغلاق ميناء، نقص سعة، تغيير لوائح) ويقدر احتماله وأثره ويخطط لمخزون احتياطي أو بدائل، والتنبؤ يوفر الطلب المتوقع الذي يجب أن تلبيه الخطط.

items.term: Case: an ocean ETA jumps by a week
items.definition: Worked case: an ocean shipment's ETA moves from 3 to 10 November between two daily reads; no reason is given on the tracking page.
items.definition_ar: حالة: موعد وصول شحنة بحرية انتقل من 3 إلى 10 نوفمبر بين قراءتين يوميتين دون ذكر سبب في صفحة التتبع.
items.scenario: Container booked on a weekly service Antwerp → Tema via a hub port. Yesterday ETA 03/11; today ETA 10/11. Vessel name on the page changed.
items.explanation: Reasoning: a one-week move equal to the service frequency, with a vessel change, fits the cargo being rolled to the next sailing (overbooking, a blank sailing, a missed cut-off) or a missed transshipment connection. It is not proof: confirm from the carrier's booking history or a schedule notice. Actions: confirm the new vessel and connection, update the customer date, check whether the free time and the order's need date are affected, and decide whether part of the order needs expediting by air.
misconceptions: Do not report 'the carrier rolled the container' as fact without the carrier saying so.

items.term: Case: demurrage caused by late original documents
terms_ar: حالة: ديمراج بسبب تأخر المستندات الأصلية
items.definition: Worked case: a container arrives on day 0 with 7 free days; the original negotiable B/L reaches the importer on day 9 through the bank.
items.definition_ar: حالة: حاوية تصل في اليوم صفر مع 7 أيام سماح، والبوليصة الأصلية القابلة للتداول تصل للمستورد في اليوم التاسع عبر البنك.
items.scenario: FOB purchase paid by letter of credit; originals sent through the banks; clearance cannot start release without the delivery order, which needs the original B/L.
items.explanation: Demurrage accrues from day 8 at least until the container is released and collected; the cause is the document path, not customs. Prevention: ask for a sea waybill or telex release where no bank needs control; or have the documents sent earlier; pre-lodge the declaration so release is immediate once the B/L arrives. Who pays depends on the contract (often the buyer under FOB).

items.term: Case: customs hold for an invoice and B/L mismatch
terms_ar: حالة: حجز جمركي لاختلاف الفاتورة عن البوليصة
items.definition: Worked case: customs holds a shipment because the invoice shows 12 packages, 3,400 kg and the B/L 14 packages, 3,900 kg.
items.definition_ar: حالة: الجمارك توقف شحنة لأن الفاتورة تذكر 12 طردًا و3400 كجم والبوليصة 14 طردًا و3900 كجم.
items.scenario: Spare parts for a dealer; the supplier added two crates after invoicing.
items.explanation: Diagnosis: the physical shipment (and B/L) is right; the invoice is incomplete. Fix: a corrected or supplementary invoice from the supplier, an amended declaration by the broker, possibly an examination. Prevention: invoice after final packing; check packing list vs invoice before shipment. Do not 'fix' it by amending the B/L to match a wrong invoice.

items.term: Case: an 'Arrived' that was not the arrival (this platform)
synonyms: arrived final destination at a city
items.definition: Real case from this platform's DHL pages: some events that read like arrival are not the arrival at destination — 'Carrier: Arrived (1st Transit Point)' at Amsterdam, and 'Arrived Final Destination' at the city of Accra days after landing (DHL's station after import clearance).
items.definition_ar: حالة حقيقية من صفحات DHL في هذه المنصة: بعض الأحداث تبدو وصولًا لكنها ليست الوصول للوجهة، مثل 'Carrier: Arrived (1st Transit Point)' في أمستردام، و'Arrived Final Destination' في مدينة أكرا بعد الهبوط بأيام (محطة DHL بعد التخليص).
items.scenario: A DHL Global Forwarding air shipment Brussels → Accra via Amsterdam.
items.explanation: Writing the transit arrival would have put an ATA days early; writing the post-clearance station would have put it 16 days late on one shipment. The rule the platform applies: the ATA is the landing at the destination airport ('Carrier: Arrived' or 'Arrived Final Destination' at an airport/port); transit points never count; when two actual arrivals conflict nothing is written and a person decides.

items.definition: Worked case: the mainline vessel reaches the hub port on time, but the container shows no loading on the planned feeder and the ETA to destination moves by 8 days.
items.definition_ar: حالة: السفينة الرئيسية تصل ميناء المحور في الموعد، لكن الحاوية لا تظهر محمّلة على السفينة المغذية المخططة ويتأخر موعد الوصول 8 أيام.
items.explanation: The first leg was fine; the delay is the connection (feeder full, yard congestion at the hub, or a late mainline arrival relative to the feeder's cut-off). Evidence to ask for: discharge at hub, loading on the next feeder. Recovery is limited once the cargo is at the hub; the lesson is about routing choice and buffer for future shipments on that lane.

items.term: Case: calculating OTIF and on-time delivery
items.definition: Worked case: 200 order lines were due in March; 170 arrived on or before the promised date, 180 arrived complete, 160 were both on time and complete.
items.definition_ar: حالة: 200 بند طلب كانت مستحقة في مارس؛ 170 وصلت في الموعد أو قبله، و180 وصلت كاملة، و160 كانت في الموعد وكاملة معًا.
items.explanation: On-time (by line) = 170 ÷ 200 = 85%. In-full = 180 ÷ 200 = 90%. OTIF (by line) = 160 ÷ 200 = 80% — it cannot be computed by multiplying 85% × 90% (76.5%) because the two failures overlap. State that it is by line, not by order.

items.term: Case: delivered in the system, but no proof of delivery
items.definition: A shipment shows 'Delivered' in the carrier's tracking, but the consignee says nothing arrived and no signed POD is available.
items.explanation: Treat the status as a claim to verify, not a fact. Ask the carrier for the POD (signature, name, time, location, photo or GPS if available); check the delivery address and whether a different site or a neighbour signed; check whether only part of the shipment was delivered. Until a POD is produced, the honest status is 'reported delivered, not confirmed'. If it was misdelivered or lost, a claim needs the notice the contract requires.

items.term: Case: an unexpected demurrage and storage invoice
items.definition: A destination invoice arrives with demurrage and storage charges the team did not expect.
items.explanation: Establish the facts before paying or disputing: discharge date, free days granted (by the carrier and by the terminal, which can differ), gate-out date, and why gate-out was late (documents, customs, delivery order, trucking). Recalculate the chargeable days with the stated counting convention. Charges caused by the carrier's own delay can be disputed; those caused by late documents usually cannot. Then fix the cause for the next shipment.

items.term: Case: OTIF dropped sharply this month
items.definition: Monthly OTIF fell from about 92% to 78% and management asks why.
items.explanation: First rule out measurement: did the definition, the data source, the order mix or the committed dates change? Then split the drop by lane, carrier, supplier, mode and failure reason (late vs short) to find where it is concentrated. A single event (a blank sailing, a customs system outage) shows as a cluster; a broad drift points to capacity or planning. Report what is measured, what is correlated and what is confirmed separately.

items.term: Case: a critical spare part for a machine that is down
items.definition: A machine at a customer site is down, waiting for a part currently on an ocean shipment due in three weeks.
items.explanation: Quantify the cost of downtime per day against the cost of options: an air shipment of a replacement part from stock elsewhere, partial air of the critical item only, expedited clearance with documents lodged before arrival, or a temporary fix. Recommend with the assumptions, the risks (availability, customs time, cost) and who must approve the extra cost. Do not promise a delivery date the carrier and customs have not confirmed.

items.term: Playbook: a shipment is late or its ETA slipped
items.definition: How to work out why a shipment is late or its ETA moved, and what to do about it.
items.explanation: A checklist for reasoning about the situation, not a finding: every cause below is a hypothesis until the evidence named next to it is seen.

facts_needed: the original and current ETA, and when each was given
where the shipment is now (last confirmed milestone and its time)
whether it is direct or via a transshipment hub
the carrier's stated reason, if any
what the delay costs (a machine down, a customer date, storage charges)

hypotheses.cause: a missed or rolled connection at a transshipment hub
hypotheses.confirm: the carrier's event shows discharge at the hub with no onward loading
hypotheses.rule_out: the next vessel/flight shows it loaded

hypotheses.cause: port congestion, weather or a blank sailing
hypotheses.confirm: carrier or terminal notices for that port/service
hypotheses.rule_out: other shipments on the same service are on time

hypotheses.cause: a customs or documentation stop
hypotheses.confirm: a hold, inspection or document query in the customs or broker status

hypotheses.cause: a tracking or data problem rather than a physical delay
hypotheses.confirm: the carrier's own site shows a later milestone than our system

next_steps.text: Confirm the last real milestone with the carrier or forwarder, with its time
Tell the customer or site the revised date only once the carrier confirms it
If the cost of waiting is high, price an alternative (air, another route)
next_steps.approval: the budget owner, before booking any extra cost

items.term: Playbook: delivered, but no proof of delivery
items.definition: How to handle a shipment shown as delivered when the consignee says it did not arrive or no POD is available.
items.explanation: A checklist for reasoning about the situation, not a finding: every cause below is a hypothesis until the evidence named next to it is seen.

facts_needed: the delivery event's time and location as the carrier recorded it
who signed, and at which address
whether the whole shipment or only part was delivered
what the contract requires as POD (signature, stamp, photo)

hypotheses.cause: delivered to a different site, gate or person
hypotheses.confirm: the POD shows another name or address
hypotheses.rule_out: the POD shows our consignee's name and address

hypotheses.cause: partly delivered
hypotheses.confirm: piece count on the POD below the shipped count

hypotheses.cause: a status entered before the delivery happened
hypotheses.confirm: no signature or GPS/photo evidence with the event

hypotheses.cause: lost or misdelivered
hypotheses.confirm: the carrier cannot produce any POD

next_steps.text: Ask the carrier in writing for the POD with signature, name, time and location
Until a POD is produced, report it as 'reported delivered, not confirmed'
If it cannot be produced, give notice of loss within the time the contract requires
next_steps.approval: whoever owns claims for this account

items.term: Playbook: customs is holding a shipment
items.definition: How to find out why customs is holding goods and what will release them.
items.explanation: A checklist for reasoning about the situation, not a finding: every cause below is a hypothesis until the evidence named next to it is seen.

facts_needed: the exact reason customs gave (from the broker or the customs system)
which documents customs has and which it asked for
whether duties and taxes have been assessed and paid
whether another agency's permit is needed
how long the goods have been held (storage and demurrage are accruing)

hypotheses.cause: a document missing or inconsistent (invoice, packing list, B/L/AWB, certificate)
hypotheses.confirm: customs' query names a document

hypotheses.cause: a classification or valuation question
hypotheses.confirm: customs proposes another HS code or value
hypotheses.rule_out: the declared code and value are accepted

hypotheses.cause: a physical inspection selected by risk management
hypotheses.confirm: an inspection order or channel shown by the broker

hypotheses.cause: duties, taxes or fees unpaid
hypotheses.confirm: an assessment awaiting payment

hypotheses.cause: another agency's permit or certificate
hypotheses.confirm: a request from that agency

next_steps.text: Get the reason in writing from the broker before acting
Send the missing or corrected document through the broker
next_steps.approval: the importer of record, if a corrected declaration is needed

next_steps.text: Ask whether release against a guarantee is possible while a value or code question is settled

items.definition: How to work through invoice, packing list and transport document differences (weights, pieces, values, descriptions).
items.explanation: A checklist for reasoning about the situation, not a finding: every cause below is a hypothesis until the evidence named next to it is seen.

facts_needed: each document's figure for the field that differs (weight, pieces, value, description)
gross versus net weight on each
units on each (kg/lb, pieces/packages)
whether one document is a house and the other a master document
what was physically shipped (packing list, loading photos, weighbridge)

hypotheses.cause: gross versus net weight, or kg versus lb
hypotheses.confirm: the difference matches packaging weight or a unit conversion
hypotheses.rule_out: the same basis is used on both

hypotheses.cause: house and master documents counting differently (consolidation)
hypotheses.confirm: the master covers more than one house shipment

hypotheses.cause: a partial shipment or split
hypotheses.confirm: another document covers the remaining pieces

hypotheses.cause: a genuine error on one document
hypotheses.confirm: the supplier or forwarder confirms and corrects it

next_steps.text: Line up the figures side by side and settle units and gross/net first
Ask the party that issued the wrong document to correct it before customs lodgement
If customs already has it, let the broker decide whether an amendment is needed

items.term: Playbook: two sources give different statuses
items.definition: How to decide what to believe when the carrier, forwarder, airline or our system disagree about a shipment's status.
items.explanation: A checklist for reasoning about the situation, not a finding: every cause below is a hypothesis until the evidence named next to it is seen.

facts_needed: each source's exact status text and its timestamp (and time zone)
the location each status refers to
which identifier each source tracks (house or master number)
when each source last updated

hypotheses.cause: one source refers to a transit point, not the destination
hypotheses.confirm: the 'arrived' location is a hub (e.g. DXB, DOH) not the destination

hypotheses.cause: one source is stale
hypotheses.confirm: its last update is older than the other's

hypotheses.cause: different identifiers (house vs master)
hypotheses.confirm: they track different numbers

hypotheses.cause: a time-zone shift moving the date
hypotheses.confirm: times differ by the zones' offset

next_steps.text: Take the most specific, most recent event from the party physically holding the goods
Do not record an ATA from a transit or non-destination event
If they still conflict, ask the carrier and record the answer

items.term: Playbook: an unexpected or disputed charge
items.definition: How to check a demurrage, detention, storage or surcharge invoice before paying or disputing it.
items.explanation: A checklist for reasoning about the situation, not a finding: every cause below is a hypothesis until the evidence named next to it is seen.

facts_needed: the dates the clock ran from and to (discharge, gate-out, empty return)
the free days granted by the carrier and by the terminal
the tariff or agreement rate and how days are counted
why the container stayed (documents, customs, delivery order, trucking)

hypotheses.cause: free time counted differently (calendar vs working days, first day counted or not)
hypotheses.confirm: recalculation with the agreed convention differs from the invoice

hypotheses.cause: terminal storage and carrier demurrage both charged for the same days
hypotheses.confirm: two invoices cover the same period for different parties

hypotheses.cause: the delay was caused by the carrier (late release, wrong documents from them)
hypotheses.confirm: carrier-side cause documented
hypotheses.rule_out: cause on our side (late documents, unpaid charges)

hypotheses.cause: the charge is correct
hypotheses.confirm: dates, free time and rate reconcile

next_steps.text: Recalculate the chargeable days with the agreed counting convention
Dispute in writing only the part that does not reconcile, with the evidence
Fix the cause for the next shipment (documents earlier, pre-arrival lodgement)

items.definition: How to explain a sudden change in OTIF, on-time delivery, cost or another KPI.
items.explanation: A checklist for reasoning about the situation, not a finding: every cause below is a hypothesis until the evidence named next to it is seen.

facts_needed: the definition and data source used in both periods
the volume in both periods (a small base swings easily)
the breakdown by lane, carrier, supplier, mode and failure reason
any one-off event in the period

hypotheses.cause: a change in definition, data source or cut-off
hypotheses.confirm: the calculation changed between periods

hypotheses.cause: a change in mix (more of a slow lane or supplier)
hypotheses.confirm: the drop is concentrated where volume grew

hypotheses.cause: a single disruption (blank sailing, strike, system outage)
hypotheses.confirm: failures cluster in dates or one carrier

hypotheses.cause: a real performance decline
hypotheses.confirm: decline across lanes with the same definition and mix

next_steps.text: Recompute both periods with the same definition before reporting a change
Report what is measured, what is correlated and what is confirmed, separately

items.definition: How to plan recovery when a late shipment stops a machine, a site or a customer commitment.
items.explanation: A checklist for reasoning about the situation, not a finding: every cause below is a hypothesis until the evidence named next to it is seen.

facts_needed: the cost per day of waiting
where the part is now and its confirmed arrival
whether stock exists elsewhere (another hub, a supplier)
the options' lead times and costs (air, partial air, local purchase)
customs time for each option at destination

hypotheses.cause: waiting for the current shipment is cheapest
hypotheses.confirm: its confirmed arrival is soon enough

hypotheses.cause: an expedited replacement is justified
hypotheses.confirm: downtime cost per day × days saved > extra freight and duty

next_steps.text: Compare downtime cost against each option's cost and time, with the assumptions written down
Lodge documents before arrival for whichever option is chosen
Book the faster option
next_steps.approval: the budget owner — extra freight is a cost decision

items.term: Playbook: a partial or short delivery
items.definition: How to handle receiving fewer pieces or units than shipped, ordered or invoiced.
items.explanation: A checklist for reasoning about the situation, not a finding: every cause below is a hypothesis until the evidence named next to it is seen.

facts_needed: pieces and quantities on the order, the invoice, the transport document and the goods receipt
whether the rest is travelling separately (offloaded, split, backordered)
whether anything was damaged or refused at delivery
what the customer needs first (a partial now, or everything together)

hypotheses.cause: the rest was offloaded or split in transit and follows on a later flight or vessel
hypotheses.confirm: the carrier shows the missing pieces on another flight or booking
hypotheses.rule_out: all pieces show on the same movement

hypotheses.cause: the supplier shipped short or backordered the balance
hypotheses.confirm: the packing list shows fewer pieces than the order
hypotheses.rule_out: packing list shows the full quantity

hypotheses.cause: lost or pilfered in transit
hypotheses.confirm: piece count dropped between two handovers with no split
hypotheses.rule_out: the count matches at every handover

hypotheses.cause: a counting or unit difference
hypotheses.confirm: packages versus pieces, or units per carton, explain it

next_steps.text: Reconcile order, invoice, packing list, transport document and receipt line by line
Pay only for what was received, or ask the supplier for a credit note
Ask whether the customer wants the partial now or waits for the rest
If pieces are lost, note it on the delivery receipt and claim in time

items.term: Playbook: rolled cargo, blank sailings and capacity
items.definition: How to respond when a booking is rolled, a sailing is cancelled or capacity tightens, and new surcharges appear.
items.explanation: A checklist for reasoning about the situation, not a finding: every cause below is a hypothesis until the evidence named next to it is seen.

facts_needed: the original and new vessel or sailing and their dates
who rolled it and why (overbooking, cut-off missed, weight)
what the booking terms say about rolling and about rate changes
which shipments are time-critical

hypotheses.cause: carrier overbooking
hypotheses.confirm: the carrier's notice cites space or overbooking
hypotheses.rule_out: the box missed the cut-off or a document

hypotheses.cause: our side missed a cut-off (documents, VGM, gate-in)
hypotheses.confirm: the gate-in or document submission was after the cut-off

hypotheses.cause: a new surcharge applies to the new sailing
hypotheses.confirm: the carrier's tariff or notice dates the surcharge to the new sailing
hypotheses.rule_out: the surcharge applies only to new bookings

next_steps.text: Ask the carrier why it was rolled and for the new sailing in writing
Check whether the rate agreement allows a surcharge on a rolled booking before accepting it
next_steps.approval: the person who owns the rate agreement

next_steps.text: Move time-critical items to another service or mode if the delay costs more
